source: docs/specs/06_events/04_endings.md (the end screen) and 01_golden_king_and_succession.md (the two-face camp names). One scripted localisation per checkpoint line (zin_loc_chronicle_cpNN), per paragraph (zin_loc_chronicle_pN), the heading, the meter, the closing line, the player's part, the lists of the lead-up events and the Lost Cause cost. A line is a string, or { text, variants: [{ if, text }], needs } where needs are the conditions under which the historical state may be shown (otherwise the diverged line stands in).

1.heading: The Fourth Age ended on [GetDateText]: the Lost Cause prevailed.
1.name: The Lost Cause

2.heading: The Fourth Age ended on [GetDateText]: the children of Volgan inherited a ruined world.
2.name: Children of Volgan

3.heading: The Fourth Age ended on [GetDateText]: the Ashen Throne was raised.
3.name: The Ashen Throne

4.heading: The Fourth Age ended on [GetDateText]: the Golden Court endured.
4.name: The Golden Court Endures

5.heading: The Fourth Age ended on [GetDateText]: a western crown held Parim.
5.name: A Western Crown in Parim

6.heading: The Fourth Age ended on [GetDateText]: Lerendor became master of the strait.
6.name: Master of the Strait

7.heading: The Fourth Age ended on [GetDateText]: the East was gathered under one crown.
7.name: One King in the East

8.heading: On [GetDateText] the chroniclers closed the Fourth Age unfinished: no crown had ended it.
8.name: The Age Unfinished

01.1: The age began in peace, in the gilded years of a king who sold his offices.

02.1: A man woke in the ice of the Cold Lands.

2.text: The man in the ice woke at an hour no one had foretold.

variants.text: The man in the ice woke early, before the world was ready for him.
The man in the ice woke late, when the world had stopped looking north.

03.1: The Truce of the Grey Ford broke, and the western clans remembered their old quarrels.
03.2: The Grey Ford truce held, and the clans kept their bows strung but quiet.

04.1: In the West he made a peace and laid a crown down.
04.2: Another hand made the western peace.

05.1: In Gaelor the Golden King died in his sleep, and Parim rang its bells for a day.

2.text: The Golden King did not die in the year the age foretold.

variants.text: The Golden King lost his kingdom while he lived, and went on living in exile.
The Golden King died in his bed in his own time, and no hand hastened him.
The Golden King did not die as the Council planned.

06.1: The temples laid the crown before [zin_loc_deliverer].
06.2: Another camp took the seals of Parim.

07.1: Storms carried the stranger to the Islands of the South.

08.1: At Gala, Lorien named him Eindil, son of Ein.
08.2: He learned his name by another road.

09.1: At Yeldenne the guardian fell and gave Glo to [zin_loc_eindil].
09.2: The hall of Yeldenne ended another way.

10.1: He warned Aenor, and Aenor called him an impostor.

11.1: The War of the Last Crowns began.

2.text: The war of the crowns began on a day the chroniclers had not foretold.

variants.text: The war of the crowns began early, before the chroniclers had finished their warnings.
The war of the crowns began late, after the chroniclers had grown tired of warning.

12.1: The North abandoned the old alliance.
12.2: The North kept, or broke, its oath in its own way.

13.1: The West crossed the wide sea.
13.2: The West did not cross as conquerors.

14.2: No eastern coalition crossed the rift.

15.1: Volgan retook Mirolon and marched north.

16.1: The dead rose out of the north.
16.2: The dead rose at another hour, or not at all.

1.text: The god-king fled east and was named King of the East; the world learned his name.

18.2: Parim did not fall to the West.

19.1: On a dragon, with Varner and Golbran, came [zin_loc_eindil] back to the war.
19.2: In the quiet after, [zin_loc_eindil] came back to no battle.
19.3: The stranger did not come back.

21.1: Volgan cast [zin_loc_eindil] down, and the New Gods raised him.

23.1: Kusven, the grave-wind of the winter tales, came forth out of the black north, and Lorien died forcing him back.
23.2: Kusven, the grave-wind of the winter tales, came forth out of the black north and withdrew without the death of the King of Gala.

1.text: Afrit came back from the East and cast his brother from a cliff.

2.text: The stranger's trial came in another shape.

variants.text: The second betrayal went another way.

1.text: In the palace the false god was stripped and killed; Golbran died saving [zin_loc_eindil].

26.1: Eindil, son of Ein, was crowned King of Aenor.
26.3: No king of Aen's line was crowned.

meter: The Gathering Dark stood at [?global.zin_gathering_dark|0] of a hundred.

unknown.zol: what the Old God keeps in the dark
unknown.tail: what the Fifth Age will be, no chronicle of this age can say.

your_part.text: The age ended in your hands. You crowned the king the league fought for, and asked no crown to kneel.
The age ended in your hands. The grave hosts hold the plains, and the clients kneel in your name.
The age ended in your hands. The temples are full, the council sits in every court, and your name is spoken as a god's.
The age ended in your hands. The feasts go on in Parim, and the gold has not run out.
The age ended in your hands. Your banners hold the oldest city of men.
The age ended in your hands. No ship crosses the Narrow Sea without passing your chain.
The age ended in your hands. One crown rules the caravan roads, and it is yours.
Your banners stood with the heir when it mattered.
The king will remember what you did for a stranger.
You knelt. History will remember to whom.
Your realm did not see the end of the war as a free crown.
The north keeps its counsel. The dead are patient.
Your realm lived through the end of an age.

possible.text: §YThe Lost Cause§!: the heir of Aen crowned in Parim.
§YChildren of Volgan§!: the Great Spirit's hosts holding Parim.
§YThe Ashen Throne§!: Afrit's temples ruling from Parim.

outcomes.text: §YThe Golden Court endures§!: the Golden King still reigns.
§YA western crown in Parim§!: western banners hold the city.
§YMaster of the Strait§!: Lerendor holds both shores.
§YOne king in the East§!: the caravan roads answer to one crown.

cost.dead_tail: did not live to see it.
cost.zol: The dead of the black north were driven back, not destroyed.
cost.volgan: Volgan's body was broken; what remains of him, no one can say.
cost.necklace: The king wears the Necklace of the Abyss, and its price is not yet known.
